newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's VA Tech sees E.Europe potential.
newsitem.headline: Austria's VA Tech sees E.Europe potential.

text.p: Austrian engineering group VA Technologie said on Friday it saw enormous business potential in Central and Eastern Europe.
VA Tech, which has orders worth 6.7 billion schillings ($543 million) currently, expected its order intake to multiply in the medium term.
"When this market begins to boom, it will offer a gigantic potential for our group", chief executive Othmar Phringer told journalists.

"In five years time we see an enormous increase in order intake", chief financial officer Helmut Hamminger said, adding that new orders could easily show a five- to sevenfold increase from an average of three billion schillings currently.
VA Tech, a leading constructor of metallurgical plants, said it could build on its long established relations with eastern European clients.
During the last 40 years VA Tech has delivered equipment worth 180 billion schillings.

The scope for future growth in the metallurgical sector was considerable. Although crude steel production in Central and Eastern Europe (excluding the Commonwealth of Independent States) has been halved since 1989, an increased volume of investment is expected in order to make the industry competitive, Phringer said.

The Russian steel industry would invest $3 billion annually and Ukraine was poised to spend some $12.5 billion to modernise the steel sector. Similar investment could be expected in Poland and other contries.
VA Tech also forecast high levels of investment in the energy sector, where efficiency and environmental standards lag far behind Western patterns.
Phringer said energy-related investment volume in the region for the period up to 2010 would total $110 billion.
Hamminger was cautious on the short-term outlook, saying the countries needed to establish functioning capital markets and to provide comprehensive business services.
-- Christian Gutlederer, Salzburg Newsroom, +43 662 87 99 43 ($ = 12.33 Austrian Schillings)
